title: Calculate radio frequency and wavelength
description: Perform mathematical calculations to determine frequency when wavelength is known, or wavelength when frequency is known, using the constant velocity of 300,000,000 meters per second.

title: Select an antenna based on mission requirements
description: Select the appropriate antenna type (HF, VHF, or UHF) and configuration based on the required range, frequency band, and mobility requirements of the MAGTF.

title: Calculate antenna length
description: Determine the physical dimensions required for an antenna based on the specific operating frequency to ensure resonance.

title: Orient an antenna for azimuth
description: Physically align a directional antenna to a specific azimuth to improve marginal communications and ensure the transmission of strong signals.

title: Connect a transceiver to an antenna
description: Directly connect a transceiver to an antenna using appropriate transmission lines, cable connectors, and baluns while minimizing energy loss.

title: Repair antenna components in the field
description: Perform field repairs on whip antennas, wire antennas, guys, and masts using available materials to restore communication capabilities.

title: Construct a field expedient antenna
description: Build functional antennas (such as an End-Fed Half-Wave or Center-Fed Doublet) using field-expedient materials and techniques for HF or VHF communications.

title: Site a SATCOM antenna
description: Select an appropriate location for satellite communications antennas, considering terrain, obstacles, and horizon angles.

title: Determine horizon angles
description: Measure or calculate the angle of the horizon at a specific site to ensure a clear line of sight for satellite or line-of-sight communications.

title: Layout an antenna farm
description: Organize the internal arrangement of multiple antennas at a command post, considering frequency bands, polarization, and power/signal line placement to minimize interference.

title: Select Single Channel Radio (SCR) equipment based on frequency requirements
description: Identify and select the appropriate radio system (HF, VHF, or UHF) and specific nomenclature (e.g., AN/PRC-104, AN/PRC-119) based on the required frequency range and mission application.

title: Establish a radio communications circuit
description: Configure a radio link consisting of a transmitter, power supply, transmission lines, antennas, and receiver to generate, radiate, and demodulate electromagnetic waves.

title: Match antenna characteristics to the propagation path
description: Select and configure an antenna that aligns with the intended propagation path (ground wave or sky wave) to maximize the signal-to-noise (S/N) ratio.

title: Evaluate terrain for surface wave conductivity
description: Assess the Earth's surface type (e.g., sea water, loamy soil, desert) to determine the relative conductivity and its impact on surface wave signal absorption.

title: Predict regular ionospheric variations for sky wave communications
description: Analyze daily, seasonal, 27-day, and 11-year sunspot cycles to anticipate changes in the ionosphere's ability to reflect radio waves.

title: Determine critical frequency for sky wave transmission
description: Identify the upper frequency limit for a specific ionized layer to ensure radio waves are reflected back to Earth at a given angle of incidence.

title: Identify irregular ionospheric disturbances
description: Recognize the signs of Sporadic E, Sudden Ionospheric Disturbances (SID), and ionospheric storms (flutter fading) to troubleshoot communication outages.

title: Calculate Line of Sight (LOS) distance for direct waves
description: Determine the maximum distance for direct wave propagation based on antenna height and atmospheric refraction/diffraction factors.

title: Adjust antenna height to control signal coverage
description: Manipulate the height of the transmitting antenna in relation to the operating frequency to control the angle of incidence and the resulting skip distance or coverage area.

title: Employ Near-Vertical Incidence Skywave (NVIS) techniques
description: Configure antenna height and transmission paths to utilize near-vertical transmission for short-range skywave communications, avoiding undesirable skip zones.

title: Select operating frequencies to mitigate fading
description: Identify and select the correct frequency and use transmitting/receiving equipment to ensure a reliable signal despite periodic increases and decreases in signal strength.

title: Determine Maximum Usable Frequency (MUF) and Lowest Usable Frequency (LUF)
description: Calculate or predict the MUF and LUF for a specific communication path based on time of day, distance, and atmospheric conditions to ensure skywave transmission is possible.

title: Generate propagation predictions using SPEED
description: Utilize the System Planning, Engineering, and Evaluation Device (SPEED) to obtain detailed propagation predictions for mission planning.

title: Select a radio site to minimize signal interference
description: Evaluate and select receiver and transmitter locations that avoid proximity to airfields, high-flying aircraft paths, and man-made objects (buildings/towers) that cause reflections or signal cancellation.

title: Establish communications using reflected wave propagation
description: Direct transmitting and receiving antennas toward a point of maximum reflection (such as a mountain or large structure) to communicate beyond normal line-of-sight distances.

title: Select antenna polarization for Line-of-Sight (LOS) paths
description: Determine and apply the appropriate polarization (vertical or horizontal) to reduce phase differences between direct and reflected waves over LOS paths.

title: Establish communications using diffraction
description: Utilize the bending of radio waves over curved surfaces or mountain ridges to communicate in the VHF and UHF ranges when a direct line-of-sight is obstructed.

title: Configure equipment for tropospheric scatter communications
description: Employ high-power transmitters (greater than 1 kW) and high-gain antennas (10 dB or more) with sensitive receivers to communicate via atmospheric 'blobs' over distances up to 500 km.

title: Mitigate manmade electromagnetic interference
description: Identify and reduce manmade noise by orienting antennas horizontally, balancing transmission lines with respect to ground, or relocating the receiving system at least one kilometer from noise sources.

title: Select antenna polarization based on frequency and propagation mode
description: Determine the required antenna polarization (vertical, horizontal, or circular) based on the frequency band (LF, MF, HF, VHF, UHF) and the intended propagation path (ground wave, sky wave, or satellite).

title: Configure antenna for ground wave transmission
description: Deploy vertically polarized antennas for medium and low frequency ground wave circuits to prevent the shorting out of horizontal lines of electric force by the Earth's surface.

title: Configure antenna for sky wave transmission
description: Deploy horizontal or vertical antennas for high frequency (HF) sky wave transmission, prioritizing horizontal antennas to achieve effective high-angle radiation and directional properties.

title: Orient antenna for maximum signal reception
description: Align the receiving antenna in the same direction as the electric field component of the incoming radio wave (matching polarization) to achieve maximum signal pickup.

title: Employ antenna directionality to minimize interference
description: Select and position antennas (omnidirectional, bidirectional, or unidirectional) to optimize signal strength to friendly units while minimizing interference from specific directions or enemy forces.

title: Balance antenna and transmission lines
description: Balance the antenna and transmission line with respect to ground to ensure noise voltages cancel at the receiver input terminals.

title: Select antenna for low frequency (LF) operations
description: Utilize a 1.5 meter tuned whip or appropriate large-signal collection antenna for frequencies below 1 MHz to overcome dominant atmospheric noise.

title: Employ narrowband antennas for interference rejection
description: Utilize narrowband antennas in crowded HF environments to reject strong interfering signals near the desired operating frequency.

title: Orient a horizontal half-wave antenna for interference reduction
description: Adjust the physical orientation of a horizontal half-wave antenna so that the ends of the antenna point directly at an interfering station to minimize undesired signals.

title: Match antenna length to operating frequency
description: Achieve resonance by physically or electronically matching the length of the antenna to the radio wave frequency to ensure effective radiation.

title: Relocate a receiving antenna to mitigate electromagnetic scattering
description: Identify and move a receiving antenna within a congested environment or building to a location where reflected and direct signals reinforce rather than cancel each other.

title: Install a ground connection for a vertical antenna
description: Establish a ground or artificial ground (counterpoise) for a vertical whip or monopole to minimize transmitter power dissipation and maximize radiation efficiency.

title: Measure antenna bandwidth
description: Determine the frequency range of an antenna by changing the frequency of a constant-strength test signal and measuring the points where power output is one-half (-3 dB) of the center frequency.

title: Select antenna take-off angle based on circuit distance
description: Configure or select an HF antenna with a high take-off angle for short-range communications or a low take-off angle for long-range communications.

title: Construct a field-expedient ground connection
description: Create a low-resistance ground connection using metal rods, existing grounded structures, underground pipe systems, or bayonets driven into the soil.

title: Treat soil to reduce antenna ground resistance
description: Apply conductive substances such as sodium chloride, calcium chloride, or magnesium sulfate to soil to improve conductivity, ensuring substances do not contaminate nearby drinking water supplies.

title: Fabricate a field-expedient ground rod
description: Construct a ground rod from pipe or conduit by cleaning the connection point with sandpaper, installing a ground clamp, and soldering or joining a ground wire protected by tape.

title: Install a wire counterpoise
description: Erect a wire device a short distance above the ground and insulated from it to serve as an artificial ground, ensuring the size is at least equal to the antenna.

title: Install a ground screen
description: Lay a large area of metal mesh or screen on the ground surface under an antenna to reduce ground absorption losses and stabilize radiation resistance.

title: Calculate physical antenna length for a half-wave antenna
description: Apply the correction factor of 0.95 to the frequency-based formula to determine the physical length in meters or feet for frequencies between 3 and 50 MHz.

title: Calculate physical length for a long-wire antenna
description: Apply the harmonic operation formula (Length = 150(N - 0.05) / Frequency) to determine the physical length of an antenna one wavelength or longer.

title: Orient an antenna using a magnetic compass
description: Determine the correct azimuth for antenna placement using a magnetic compass and a magnetic declination map to account for variation from true north.

title: Troubleshoot marginal radio communications
description: Perform a sequence of corrective actions including checking cable couplings, retuning equipment, adjusting antenna height, and relocating antennas to improve circuit quality.

title: Match transmission line impedance to antenna load
description: Select and connect transmission lines that match the characteristic impedance of the load to ensure maximum energy transfer and minimize reflections.

title: Match transmission line impedance by length
description: Calculate and cut a transmission line to specific wavelength intervals (half-wavelength) to match antenna to transceiver when impedances differ significantly.

title: Match an end-fed long-wire antenna
description: Feed a long-wire antenna using a quarter-wavelength section of wire to achieve an impedance match between the transmitter and the antenna.

title: Connect a balanced antenna to coaxial cable
description: Route coaxial cable perpendicular to dipole wires for a distance greater than one-half the dipole length and verify total cable length to prevent unwanted RF induction.

title: Connect an unbalanced antenna to twin-lead
description: Identify and connect the hot and ground terminals of a transmitter to the corresponding conductors of a twin-lead line to feed an unbalanced antenna.

title: Reduce twin-lead transmission line radiation
description: Twist twin-lead transmission line into a helix with approximately one twist every 30 centimeters to prevent radiation and reduce noise pickup.

title: Install transmission line connectors
description: Prepare cable ends and solder fittings onto standard transmission lines to facilitate rapid assembly and disassembly of communications systems.

title: Employ a balun in an antenna system
description: Install a field-constructed or manufactured balun at the antenna or transceiver to transform energy between balanced and unbalanced devices.

title: Select an HF antenna site
description: Identify an antenna location that avoids scattering objects and maintains an optimum height of approximately 0.4 wavelength above electrical ground.

title: Determine HF antenna take-off angles
description: Calculate the required take-off angle for sky wave propagation based on circuit distance and time of day using standardized propagation tables.

title: Select an HF antenna based on propagation mode
description: Choose between vertically polarized antennas for ground wave or high-gain directional antennas for sky wave based on mission requirements and circuit distance.

title: Determine antenna coverage requirements
description: Analyze the radio circuit type (mobile/vehicular vs. point-to-point) to identify the required radiation pattern (omnidirectional, bidirectional, or directional).

title: Determine antenna take-off angle
description: Calculate the required take-off angle based on distance and time of day (Daytime vs. Nighttime F2 Region) using Table 4-1.

title: Inventory antenna construction materials
description: Examine and verify the availability of necessary construction materials, such as supports and wire, prior to antenna selection.

title: Determine support requirements for a horizontal dipole
description: Identify the number of supports required for a horizontal dipole based on the operating frequency (e.g., requiring a third center support for frequencies of 5 MHz or less).

title: Perform antenna site survey
description: Examine the proposed antenna site to ensure the physical dimensions of the selected antenna will fit within the available space.

title: Calculate antenna length for field-expedient antennas
description: Determine the physical length of antenna elements in feet based on the operating frequency using the standard formula (468 / Frequency in MHz for half-wave dipoles).

title: Construct a field-expedient half-wave dipole antenna
description: Assemble a horizontal antenna using wire, insulators, and a transmission line, ensuring the two elements are cut to the correct length for the assigned frequency.

title: Construct a field-expedient long-wire antenna
description: Install a wire radiator that is at least one wavelength long, supported by available structures, to provide directional gain and improved signal strength.

title: Construct a field-expedient vertical whip antenna
description: Create a vertical radiator using wire and a support structure (such as a tree or pole) to facilitate omnidirectional ground-wave communications.

title: Fabricate field-expedient antenna insulators
description: Use non-conductive materials such as plastic, glass, or dry wood to isolate antenna elements from support structures and prevent signal grounding.

title: Orient a field-expedient antenna for maximum radiation
description: Position the antenna broadside or end-on relative to the receiving station based on the specific radiation pattern of the antenna type used.

title: Ground a field-expedient antenna system
description: Establish an electrical connection to the earth using ground stakes or radial wires to improve antenna efficiency and operator safety.

title: Apply the Systems Approach to Training (SAT) methodology
description: Utilize the structured methodology for developing military training as defined in USMC standards.

title: Execute the ADDIE model for curriculum development
description: Perform the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation phases of the training development cycle.

title: Create Training and Readiness (T&R) events
description: Develop standardized T&R events in accordance with Marine Corps manual standards.

title: Write learning objectives in Mager format
description: Construct Terminal Learning Objectives (TLO) and Enabling Learning Objectives (ELO) using the Condition, Behavior, and Standard format.

title: Classify learning objectives using Bloom's Taxonomy
description: Assign cognitive level classifications to learning objectives to ensure appropriate training depth and measurable standards.

title: Extract trainable tasks from source material
description: Analyze source documentation to identify discrete, observable, job-relevant, and trainable procedures or skills.

title: Establish traceability between training artifacts
description: Ensure a logical link exists between T&R events, TLOs, ELOs, and final performance assessments.

title: Identify Radio Frequency (RF) radiation hazards
description: Recognize and identify potential RF radiation hazard areas based on equipment type, power output, and antenna configuration to ensure personnel safety.

title: Implement RF safety precautions
description: Establish safety perimeters, post standardized RF hazard warning signs, and maintain safe separation distances from active transmitting antennas.

title: Construct a wire antenna
description: Measure, cut, and assemble wire elements, insulators, and feed lines to create a functional antenna system according to technical specifications.

title: Install antenna insulators
description: Properly attach insulators to antenna wire ends and support lines to ensure electrical isolation from ground and support structures.

title: Connect an antenna feed line
description: Attach the transmission line to the antenna driven element ensuring proper impedance matching and secure physical connection.

title: Assemble a Manpack Radio System
description: Physically integrate the radio receiver-transmitter, battery box, handset, and antenna into a functional manpack configuration.

title: Install a Radio Antenna
description: Attach the specified antenna to the radio's antenna connector, ensuring a secure physical and electrical connection.

title: Connect a Handset to a Radio Set
description: Connect the H-250/U or equivalent handset to the audio/data connector on the radio's interface panel.

title: Connect a Power Source to a Radio Set
description: Mate the battery box or external power cable to the radio set to provide electrical power for operation.

title: Operate tactical radio interface controls
description: Utilize the keypad and display interface to navigate menus, select options, and input data into the tactical radio system.

title: Select radio frequency presets
description: Use the 'PRE' button and directional arrows to cycle through and select programmed frequency presets as indicated on the display.

title: Adjust radio audio and squelch settings
description: Modify the volume and squelch levels using the dedicated 'SQL' button and interface controls to ensure clear voice reception.

title: Toggle encryption modes (CT/PT)
description: Switch the radio between Cipher Text (CT) and Plain Text (PT) modes to secure or unsecure communications based on operational requirements.

title: Transmit tactical text messages
description: Navigate to the 'TEXT' menu option to compose, send, and read data messages via the tactical radio network.

title: Monitor GPS status and data
description: Access the 'GPS' menu function to view current position data and satellite synchronization status.

title: Configure radio system settings
description: Access the 'SYSTEM' menu to modify device configurations, network parameters, and operational modes.

title: Initiate a radio call
description: Use the 'CALL' button to initiate voice or data transmissions to a specific net or station.

title: Calculate antenna length for a specific frequency
description: Determine the physical length of an antenna element using the standard formula (468/frequency in MHz for a half-wave dipole) to ensure resonance.

title: Construct a field-expedient inverted vee antenna
description: Erect a wire antenna in an inverted 'V' configuration using a single central support to provide omnidirectional radiation patterns.

title: Repair broken antenna wire
description: Perform a Western Union splice or use field-expedient connectors to restore electrical continuity to a damaged antenna element.

title: Improvise antenna insulators
description: Identify and utilize non-conductive materials such as plastic, glass, or dry wood to isolate antenna elements from grounding sources.

title: Construct a field-expedient vertical antenna
description: Utilize a vertical support and a ground-plane radial system to construct an antenna for ground-wave communication.

title: Splice coaxial cable
description: Repair damaged transmission lines by stripping insulation, joining center conductors, and restoring the shield braid to maintain signal integrity.

title: Develop a Communications Plan
description: Formulate a comprehensive plan to support command and control requirements, including the integration of various communication systems and networks.

title: Determine Communication Requirements
description: Analyze the mission and operational environment to identify specific voice, data, and video communication needs for the unit.

title: Implement Communications Security (COMSEC) Measures
description: Apply procedures and safeguards to protect telecommunications and ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information.

title: Coordinate Communications Support with External Units
description: Liaise with higher, adjacent, and subordinate units to ensure interoperability and seamless communication across the area of operations.

title: Manage Frequency Assignments
description: Allocate and monitor radio frequencies to prevent interference and optimize the use of the electromagnetic spectrum.

title: Exercise Communications Control (COMMCON)
description: Direct and supervise the technical operation and maintenance of the communications system to ensure it meets operational requirements.

title: Maintain Communication Logs
description: Record all significant communication events, message traffic, and system status updates in accordance with established protocols.

title: Operate the radio function switch
description: Manipulate the main function knob to switch between OFF, Cipher Text (CT), Plain Text (PT), Load (LD), and Zeroize (Z) positions.

title: Select radio waveforms from System Presets
description: Navigate the LCD menu using the keypad to select specific waveforms including VHF/UHF LOS, SATCOM, P25, HPW, ANW2, and SRW.

title: Adjust radio squelch settings
description: Utilize the SQL (Squelch) key on the tactical keypad to adjust or toggle the receiver squelch threshold.

title: Manage radio display lighting
description: Use the LT (Light) key to adjust the LCD backlight and keypad illumination for day or night operations.

title: Zeroize the radio
description: Perform emergency or routine clearing of all COMSEC and variables by rotating the function switch to the 'Z' position.

title: Connect radio peripherals
description: Properly seat and secure audio handsets to the J1 connector or data cables to the J2 connector.

title: Access radio options and modes
description: Use the OPT (Options) and MODE keys to navigate sub-menus for advanced configuration and operational mode changes.

title: Connect Peripherals to the AN/PRC-150(C)
description: Properly attach the antenna, handset (H-250), and power source to the respective ANT, AUDIO, and POWER connectors on the front panel.

title: Power On the AN/PRC-150(C) Radio Set
description: Rotate the Function Switch from the OFF position to the desired operational mode, such as PT (Plain Text) or CT (Cipher Text).

title: Zeroize the AN/PRC-150(C) Radio Set
description: Perform emergency destruction of cryptographic variables by rotating the Function Switch to the Z-ALL position.

title: Configure Radio Settings via Front Panel Keypad
description: Utilize the alphanumeric keypad, 'PGM' (Program), and 'ENT' (Enter) keys to navigate menus and input frequency or net data into the radio memory.

title: Prepare the AN/PRC-150(C) for COMSEC Loading
description: Set the Function Switch to the LD (Load) position to enable the transfer of cryptographic keys from a fill device via the AUDIO/DATA ports.

title: Ground the AN/PRC-150(C) Radio Set
description: Connect a tactical ground wire to the GND terminal on the radio chassis to ensure operator safety and equipment protection.

title: Perform Preventive Maintenance Checks and Services (PMCS) on Radio Equipment
description: Inspect the radio chassis, connectors, and accessories for physical damage, corrosion, and cleanliness to ensure operational readiness.

title: Install Radio Batteries
description: Properly align, seat, and secure the battery pack to the radio receiver-transmitter to provide power for operations.

title: Connect Radio Antennas
description: Attach the appropriate antenna (whip, blade, or external) to the RF connector and ensure a secure physical connection for signal transmission.

title: Operate Radio Controls and Indicators
description: Navigate the radio interface using the keypad and display to monitor status and adjust basic operating parameters.

title: Clean Radio Connectors and Ports
description: Use approved cleaning materials to remove dirt and debris from electrical contact points to prevent signal degradation.

title: Assemble a Manpack Radio Configuration
description: Integrate the receiver-transmitter, battery box, and antenna into a single man-portable unit ready for tactical employment.
